Do age and form matter at Cheltenham? Final day of the November Meeting.
Chases by age, share of runs that won: 5yo 15.7% \(18 of 115\), 6yo 15.8% \(77 of 486\), 7yo 11.4% \(105 of 918\), 8yo 8.9% \(82 of 924\), 9yo 7.2% \(51 of 708\), 10 and older 5.8% \(52 of 899\).
Hurdles by age: 4yo 7.4% \(45 of 608\), 5yo 11.1% \(94 of 846\), 6yo 9.3% \(101 of 1,090\), 7yo 7.0% \(47 of 671\), 8yo 6.0% \(24 of 401\), 9yo 4.2% \(10 of 239\), 10 and older 3.0% \(6 of 198\).
Won last time out: hurdles 12.2% \(160 of 1,312\) v 6.4% for the rest; chases 13.7% \(130 of 949\) v 8.2%.
Chases by days since last run: under 30 days 9.6%, 30 to 89 days 10.3%, off for 90 days or more 7.6%.
Course-and-distance winners won 14.9% of their chase runs \(57 of 383\) v 9.0% for the rest.
Thanks for following our Cheltenham week.

Who trains the Cheltenham winners? Day 2 of the November Meeting.
Most chase wins at Cheltenham: W P Mullins 29 \(from 169 runs\), Nicky Henderson 23 \(134\), Dan Skelton 23 \(181\), Paul Nicholls 20 \(178\), Henry de Bromhead 19 \(132\).
Most hurdle wins: Nicky Henderson 35 \(260\), W P Mullins 30 \(344\), Dan Skelton 29 \(217\), Gordon Elliott 19 \(238\), then Henry de Bromhead 15 \(107\) and Fergal O'Brien 15 \(153\).
Best strike rate of the leading trainers over hurdles \(top 12 by wins, 30 or more runs\): Emma Lavelle 20.5% \(8 from 39\).
Most hurdle winners \(jockeys\): Harry Skelton, 27 from 166 rides.

It's race day. Can Jonbon win a third Shloer Chase at Cheltenham today \(2:20\)?
Distance: around 2 miles he has won 17 of 24, never worse than 2nd.
Course: Cheltenham is his toughest track, 2 wins from 8. Both came in this race \(2023 and 2024\), and he was 2nd the other six times.
Ground: good, good to soft in places. On good ground he has won 5 of 7.
The questions: he's 10 now, he hasn't run for 246 days, and he was beaten in this race last year.
He takes on three rivals: Gidleigh Park, Saint Segal and Mighty Bandit.
The ZANS scorecard: distance, jockey and ground tick. Course and age are the questions.
Up the Jonbon!

Can you win from the back at Cheltenham? Day 1 of the November Meeting.
Win rate by running style at Cheltenham, Jan 2019 to Mar 2026:
2-mile chases: led 21.1% \(12 of 57\), prominent 13.8% \(20 of 145\), held up 3.3% \(4 of 123\). The UK and Ireland held-up average is 8.4%.
2m 4½f chases: led 15.9% \(14 of 88\), prominent 9.9% \(28 of 282\), held up 3.5% \(9 of 255\). The UK and Ireland held-up average is 8.0%.
2m ½f hurdles: led 16.7% \(11 of 66\), prominent 7.8% \(19 of 244\), held up 3.1% \(8 of 259\).
Coming from the back is hard here: in 2m and 2m 4½f chases and 2m ½f hurdles, held-up horses won only about 3%. In 3m 1½f chases held-up horses won 8 of 48 runs \(16.7%\), but that's only 35 races.

Data: Jan 2019 to Mar 2026, ZANS results database. Running style is read from the published race comments. Race-action images are AI illustrations.

Jonbon has a new jockey. Harry Cobden rides him for the first time in the Shloer Chase at Cheltenham on Friday \(2:20\).
Out goes Nico de Boinville, who rode him 14 times. In comes Harry Cobden, riding him for the first time.
Does he need Nico? With Nico he won 10 of 14. With other jockeys, also 10 of 14. Exactly the same.
Cobden knows Cheltenham: 26 winners from 179 rides here \(2023 to May 2026\), and British champion jump jockey in 2023/24.
The big one: 28 races, and Jonbon has never finished worse than 2nd.
Tomorrow: can he win a third Shloer? Up the Jonbon!

Do favourites deliver at Cheltenham? Across every Cheltenham jumps race from January 2019 to March 2026 \(ZANS results database, joint favourites left out\), the clear favourite won about 1 in 3: hurdles 32.5% \(103 of 317 races with a clear favourite\), chases 32.2% \(113 of 351\).
Ground changes the picture: hurdle favourites won 40.0% on Good but 25.6% on Good to Soft.

Know the track: Cheltenham in 55 seconds. The November Meeting runs Friday 13 to Sunday 15 November.
We looked at 770 Cheltenham National Hunt races \(341 hurdles, 386 chases, 43 bumpers\) \(Jan 2019 to Mar 2026, ZANS results database\). The fences stand out: 6.3% of chase runners fell or unseated their rider \(256 of 4,056\), against 3.1% over hurdles \(131 of 4,168\), rising to 8.1% in chases on soft ground \(115 of 1,412\).
A new Cheltenham stat every day until Sunday.
